title: AI diagram generator — describe it, get an editable diagram
excerpt: Turn a sentence into a real diagram: architecture, flowchart, sequence or org chart, on your brand, exported as SVG, PNG or editable PowerPoint. Nothing is dropped to make it fit, and the same description draws the same diagram.
content_html:
Or drop one you already have

.dgm · .vsdx · .tldraw · .drawio · .excalidraw · .mermaid
up to 8 MB · nothing is stored

A screenshot works too — PNG, JPEG or WebP, read by a model rather than parsed. On the paid plans.

Needs an account

Sign in to draw it

Free account · converting a file needs none

Your file is read once to draw the diagram and is never stored. Converting turns on anonymous usage analytics — we never send your file, its contents or your brand URL. What we measure

What you type, and what comes back

Drawn by this pipeline, not picked to flatter it. The description above each one is the whole input.

All 53 types, one worked example each →

Why these come out different

Most text-to-diagram tools hand the whole job to the model: it decides the content and draws the picture. That is why their output has a look, why the same description gives you a different diagram each time, and why a large one quietly loses boxes — the drawing is done against a fixed ladder, and what will not fit is dropped.

Here the model does one job — turning your sentence into structure — and our own layout engine draws it. So an architecture diagram with sixty services keeps sixty services, the same description gives the same diagram every time, and what comes out looks like the rest of your documents rather than like something that was generated.

No node limit
Nothing is dropped to make a diagram fit. A subnet missing from a network diagram is not a simpler diagram, it is a wrong one.

Same input, same output
Everything after the one model call is deterministic, so a diagram going into a document under review does not change under it.

Editable when it lands
PowerPoint export carries real shapes and live text. Correct a label in the deck without coming back here.

Already have the diagram? Converting one is free and needs no account →

Questions people actually ask

What do I type?
A sentence or two of plain description — who does what, in what order, and what talks to what. Naming the arrangement you want ("one row per team", "left to right by stage") is the single thing that most changes the result, because it is the part a description usually leaves out.

Will it drop parts of a big diagram?
No. The model is only asked to turn your sentence into structure; the drawing is done by our own layout engine, which has no node limit. Generators that redraw with the model itself work against a fixed ladder and quietly drop what will not fit — on a network or a process that is not a simpler diagram, it is a wrong one.

Do I get the same diagram twice from the same description?
Yes. Everything after the one model call is deterministic, so re-running a description gives the identical drawing. That matters when the diagram is going into a document somebody reviews.

Can I change what comes back?
Click any shape to correct its type or colour, restyle the whole thing against your brand, and export to PowerPoint as real editable shapes with live text — not a picture you cannot fix a typo in.

Is it free?
Converting a diagram you already have is free and needs no account. Drawing one from a description costs us a model call per press, so it needs a free account and spends 20 credits from the monthly allowance.
